stem_en:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R:
Assertion A: Helium is used to dilute oxygen in diving apparatus.
Reason R: Helium has high solubility in $\mathrm{O_2}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

statements.label: Assertion A
statements.text: Helium is used to dilute oxygen in diving apparatus.

options_en.1: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options_en.2: Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
options_en.3: A is true but R is false.
options_en.4: A is false but R is true.

subject: Chemistry

notes: every change made by a previous run of this script was reverted before re-running it: the first merge keyed Assertion-Reason questions on their boilerplate stem and their four standard options alone, which are identical across every such question in the paper, and so merged unrelated questions together. paper_codes was restored to the single code this record's source_file names; every other code on it had been added by that merge
option_order_by_code recorded for E2: each code's printed option numbers mapped onto this row's order, so one official answer can be checked against every code's key

official_answer filled from the key grid(s) for E2; all of them select the same option text after each code's option order is mapped onto this row, so the answer is corroborated across codes rather than taken from one grid

subject set to Chemistry from the printed position (question 69 of code E2); NEET's sections are 1-50 Physics, 51-100 Chemistry, 101-200 Biology and the codes reshuffle only within a section. This mapping agrees with every row in the bank that already carries a subject (617 of 617) and was not used where one was present
